subject: Subprocessor roster and APAC onshore-fallback confirmation for Neoteric
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@neoteric.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@neoteric.com, dpo@neoteric.com, procurement@neoteric.com
Date: 2028-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: current subprocessor roster + APAC residency question

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal team requested a formal, itemised list of Redwood's subprocessors involved in processing Neoteric customer data (production and telemetry), with:
- subprocessor name
- purpose (e.g., telemetry, logging, CDN)
- countries where data is processed
- transfer mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, onshore fallback)
- contract start date

We are particularly focused on APAC residency: can you confirm which subprocessors process or reasonably may process Neoteric data within APAC, and whether Redwood has any onshore fallback options for APAC customers?

If possible, please send a CSV and a simple dataflow diagram. We may need this for our internal export-control checklist by next Wednesday.

Attachments: none

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Patel
Legal & Privacy, Neoteric Analytics

Date: 2028-05-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster + APAC residency question

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear ask.

I'm looping in Kim (privacy ops) and Laura (platform ops) so we can pull the authoritative roster and the APAC mapping. High-level notes up front:
- We maintain a canonical subprocessor roster and CSV that we refresh weekly and can share with an NDA/portal link.
- For APAC, we have a mix: regional CDN and observability partners with limited edge processing, plus a backup onshore routing option in Singapore for certain customers under enterprise commitments.
- Transfer mechanisms vary by partner — most modern partners accept SCCs; a few are covered by adequacy or SOC attestations.

We'll return a CSV and a simplified dataflow diagram by EOD tomorrow. If you can share a short list of fields your procurement/legal needs (or a sample CSV), we'll align formats.

Regards,
Marcus
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Subprocessor roster - draft CSV and APAC notes

Forwarding our draft export. See attached CSV and a quick APAC flow diagram. Notes inline:

- subprocessor_roster_neoteric_request.csv (attached) contains columns: provider_name, role, data_types, countries, transfer_mechanism, contract_start, onshore_fallback_available, comments
- APAC specifics: CDNEdgeCo (Singapore, Australia) — edge caching only; ObserviSys (Hong Kong) — telemetry samplers, pseudonymised; TransitFlow (US, EU) — no APAC processing unless routed for debugging, but Singapore onshore routing is possible under Dedicated contracts.
- Onshore fallback: available as a configurable routing policy for customers on Dedicated or Private modes; for Hosted customers we offer an APAC-region instance with regional caching but cannot guarantee 100% onshore residency for telemetry without a Dedicated commitment.

[Attachment: subprocessor_roster_neoteric_request.csv]
[Attachment: apac_dataflow_map.pdf]

Happy to jump on a call if you want line-by-line mapping.

- Kim

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@neoteric.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Subprocessor roster - draft CSV and APAC notes

Thanks Kim — the CSV looks good as a first pass. A few follow-ups from our DPO/legal: 
1) For ObserviSys (HK) can you confirm whether full request/response payloads are ever sent outside the region for debugging? If yes, are they truncated/pseudonymised?
2) For TransitFlow, please specify the default data egress path and the exact condition that would trigger temporary routing to a non-APAC region.
3) Can Redwood provide a signed attestation (simple one-page) confirming the current roster and that the CSV is accurate as of the date of signing?

We also need a one-off machine-readable CSV that lists the applicable transfer legal basis per subprocessor (SCCs / adequacy / other) — it's okay to supply SCCs as "accepted" where applicable.

We'd like to target a final deliverable for our audit by EOD Tuesday (2028-05-16). Will you be able to get the attestation + the transfer-basis CSV by then?

Regards,
Aisha
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@neoteric.com>, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-05-16T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster and APAC onshore-fallback confirmation for Neoteric

Hi Aisha — thanks for the precision. We attached the two deliverables you asked for: 1) redwood_response_subprocessors.csv (machine-ready roster with transfer_basis column populated) and 2) a one-page attestation PDF (signed by our Head of Trust).

Quick answers inline to your three points:
1) ObserviSys (HK): payloads are pseudonymised by default; full payloads are only routed outside APAC for on-call debugging and are subject to access controls and manual approval. We have logged examples going back 12 months; we can extract redacted examples if required.
2) TransitFlow: default egress is EU/US (primary peering points) — temporary routing occurs only under degraded peering or targeted maintenance and is governed by our incident runbook; customers on Dedicated can opt into Singapore primary egress.
3) Attestation: attached and signed. Date-stamped: 2028-05-16.

Attachments: [redwood_response_subprocessors.csv] [Redwood_Attestation_Neoteric_20280516.pdf]
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/NEO-4552

If you want a short review call tomorrow 10am SGT, we can have Kim and an engineer join.

Best,
Laura
